findings.title: The opening name orients the commanded speech
findings.claim: Placed before the imperative to speak, Allah's name gives the coming declaration a named authority and a direction: the utterance begins under that designation.
findings.mechanism: The prepositional phrase bi-smi Allah carries the word for name and the divine proper name. In 109:1, the explicit command qul supplies the imminent speech act. Their contact lets the raised-designation and direction facets frame the commanded utterance under the named referent.
findings.reader_payoff: The refusal that follows can be heard as a declaration issued from a named frame, with its direction visible before the boundary unfolds.
findings.containment: This is a contextual relation inferred from sequence, not a grammatical claim that qul marks a source or goal, and not a claim that ism lexically means authority or direction. The focus phrase remains an invocation in Allah's name.

epistemic.reason: Trusted cross-run evidence and legacy reader accounts point to the same contact, while the direction facet under root_000743/B011 has qualified identity and is applied only as a contextual frame.

findings.title: The named referent remains available through the worship clauses
findings.claim: The repeated worship clauses let the opening name Allah serve as a possible referential pole for the speaker's otherwise unspecified object of worship.
findings.mechanism: Allah remains the focus carrier as a proper name. In 109:2–5, repeated worship verbs place speaker and addressees in a worship relation while leaving the object in the nonspecific form ma. The focus name and those acts meet as a possible named pole without a grammatical equation between them.
findings.reader_payoff: The later object phrases can be heard against the divine name already given at the opening, so the declaration has a possible named pole across its repeated contrasts.
findings.containment: This is a contextual reference, not a claim that grammar makes every ma refer to Allah or that the proper noun takes on the lexical sense of a generic worshipped being.

epistemic.reason: The worship pattern and focus name are supplied, but the connection between them is explicitly abductive and preserves the unresolved reference of each ma.

findings.title: Mercy colors the manner of a firm separation
findings.claim: The opening mercy lends the later refusal a measured manner, while the repeated denials and final your/my division keep the religious boundary intact.
findings.mechanism: The focus epithets carry active mercy and beneficence. In 109:2–5, repeated negations deny reciprocal worship; 109:6 then states the split as your religion and my religion. Their contact lets mercy color how the boundary is voiced without erasing its content.
findings.reader_payoff: A firm separation becomes perceptible within a frame of restraint, with mercy affecting the manner of refusal while the line remains clear.
findings.containment: The context does not explicitly say that mercy motivates the refusal or make worship interchangeable; the claim is a contextual effect on manner, not a cancellation of the stated boundary.

epistemic.reason: The denials and final division are explicit, while the role of mercy in regulating their manner is an inferred macro relation supported by both trusted and unbound readings.
